Go stdlib crypto/x509 DoS vulnerability (GO-2026-4947). Detected in the compiled lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) binary built with Go 1.25.8. govulncheck symbol-level analysis confirms the vulnerable code paths are not called by lpm. Fix: DAT-22804 bumps Go to 1.25.9 in liquibase-package-manager, eliminating the vulnerability at the source.

statements.status_notes: Validating certificate chains which use policies is unexpectedly inefficient when certificates in the chain contain a very large number of policy mappings, possibly causing denial of service. This only affects validation of otherwise trusted certificate chains, issued by a root CA in the VerifyOptions.Roots CertPool, or in the system certificate pool.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib crypto/x509 certificate policy mapping DoS vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.9 and 1.26.2. Current Docker builds install lpm 0.3.3 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and liquibase-package-manager v0.3.3 declares go 1.25.9 (liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3), which includes the fix.

Go stdlib internal/syscall/unix Root.Chmod symlink traversal vulnerability. Detected in the compiled lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) binary built with Go 1.25.8. govulncheck symbol-level analysis confirms the vulnerable code paths are not called by lpm. Fix: DAT-22804 bumps Go to 1.25.9 in liquibase-package-manager, eliminating the vulnerability at the source.

statements.status_notes: If one side of the TLS connection sends multiple key update messages post-handshake in a single record, the connection can deadlock, causing uncontrolled consumption of resources. This can lead to a denial of service. This only affects TLS 1.3.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib crypto/tls TLS 1.3 key update DoS vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.9 and 1.26.2. Current Docker builds install lpm 0.3.3 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and liquibase-package-manager v0.3.3 declares go 1.25.9 (liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3), which includes the fix.

statements.status_notes: When using LookupCNAME with the cgo DNS resolver, a very long CNAME response can trigger a double-free of C memory and a crash.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib LookupCNAME double-free in the cgo DNS resolver when processing a very long CNAME response. lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) is the Go binary in the Docker image; it downloads Liquibase extension driver JARs from GitHub release assets via HTTP. lpm never calls LookupCNAME — standard HTTP hostname resolution uses LookupIPAddr/LookupHost, not the CNAME-specific API. Additionally, the vulnerability requires the cgo DNS resolver, which is not the default on Linux; the pure-Go DNS resolver is active in the eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble container.

statements.status_notes: When processing HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames, transport will enter an infinite loop of writing CONTINUATION frames if it receives a SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE with a value of 0.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib HTTP/2 transport infinite loop when a server sends SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE with a value of 0. lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) is the Go binary in the Docker image; it makes HTTP/2 connections to GitHub release servers to download Liquibase extension driver JARs. Exploitation requires a server to send the malformed SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE=0 frame. lpm only connects to trusted GitHub release CDN endpoints (URLs and checksums fixed in docker/Dockerfile:35-55); no attacker- controlled server endpoint exists in lpm's execution path.

statements.status_notes: Well-crafted inputs reaching ParseAddress, ParseAddressList, and ParseDate were able to trigger excessive CPU exhaustion and memory allocations.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib net/mail CPU exhaustion via pathological inputs to ParseAddress, ParseAddressList, and ParseDate. lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) is the Go binary in the Docker image. lpm is a package manager for Liquibase extension drivers and has no email processing functionality. The vulnerable net/mail parsing functions are not called by lpm at any point during package installation or management operations.

statements.status_notes: The Dial and LookupPort functions panic on Windows when provided with an input containing a NUL (0).
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib Dial and LookupPort panic vulnerability requires Windows when processing input containing a NUL byte. The assessed Liquibase Secure Docker image uses the Linux base image eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (docker/Dockerfile:2), so the vulnerable Windows runtime environment is absent.

statements.status_notes: Pathological inputs could cause DoS through consumePhrase when parsing an email address according to RFC 5322.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib net/mail DoS via pathological email address inputs reaching the consumePhrase parser (RFC 5322 phrase parsing). lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) is the Go binary in the Docker image. lpm is a package manager for Liquibase extension drivers and has no email processing functionality. The vulnerable net/mail consumePhrase code path is not reachable from any lpm operation.
